units.source_text: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and electrocardiogram (ECG). Heart-pumping assessment with an echo or multigated acquisition (heart pumping) scan (MUGA) scan if over 65 or clinically indicated; doxorubicin requires left ventricular ejection fraction (heart pumping measurement) (LVEF) above 50%. Hearing assessment and measured kidney clearance when indicated.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Doxorubicin is given slowly into a vein over about 15 minutes, cisplatin over 2 hours, then cyclophosphamide over 30 minutes. Cisplatin requires prescribed intravenous fluids before and after treatment, so the visit takes longer than the drug infusion times. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage around the line.
units.reason: The complete source statement occurs in current consolidated narrative under approved acronym normalization.

units.source_text: Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.

units.source_heading: Methotrexate: head and neck cancer: treatment and checks
units.source_text: Methotrexate 40 mg/m² by intravenous bolus on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. There is no scheduled Day-22 dose. The clinician may increase to 50 mg/m² only if there has been no mucositis.
